title: Min-Cost Package Distribution
statement:
There are `n` houses numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Delivering a package directly to house `i` costs `cost[i]`. Some pairs of houses are **connected**. When a package is delivered to a house, every house connected to it, directly or through a chain of connected houses, also receives the package at no extra cost.

Find the minimum total cost of deliveries so that **every** house receives a package.

The list of connections may contain duplicates and self-connections (a house connected to itself); these have no special meaning.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`.
The second line contains `n` integers `cost[0..n-1]`.
Each of the next `m` lines contains two integers `a` and `b` (0-indexed): houses `a` and `b` are connected.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the minimum total delivery cost.

examples.explanation: Houses {0, 1, 2} form one group (cheapest house costs 3), houses {3, 4} form another (cheapest costs 2) and house 5 is alone (cost 4). Total 3 + 2 + 4 = 9.
No houses are connected, so every house needs its own delivery: 7 + 7 + 1 + 5 = 20.
All houses form a single chain, so one delivery to the cheapest house (cost 10) reaches everyone.

hints: A package reaches exactly the houses in the same connected component as the house it is delivered to.
Group the houses into connected components, for example with a disjoint-set union (union-find) over the connections.
Within a component you only need one delivery, so pick its cheapest house; then sum the minimum of each component.
